decision: How should a tenant brand override be modelled in WF-138?

state.change: A brand belongs to an account and carries tenant token overrides. A room joins a brand and inherits the brand's current tokens. White-label mode swaps the owner identity presented to a buyer.
state.question: What is a tenant brand override allowed to contain?
state.option_a_token_to_token: An override maps one of this product's own semantic tokens to another one, for example {accent: accent-bright}. The pair renders on the branded host as --color-accent: var(--color-accent-bright). The four tokens that decide text contrast (background, surface, foreground, muted-foreground) are locked at both ends: a tenant may neither override them nor point another token at them.
state.option_b_colour_values: An override stores validated colour values per token, reusing WF-017's is_valid_colour grammar, for example {accent: '#22c55e'}.
state.option_c_stylesheet: An override stores custom properties or a stylesheet supplied by the tenant.
evidence_for_a: The issue is explicit: 'Token names, not raw hex' and 'Model the override as a token-to-token mapping.'

docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md: 'Style with semantic tokens. Never with a raw hex value ... Because tokens live in one file, a palette change lands everywhere at once. If you hardcode a colour you have opted out of that, permanently.'
The design system states 4.5:1 text contrast and a locked light theme as the floor, so the four tokens that decide contrast have to stay the product's.
frontend/src/index.css declares every colour as --color-<token>, so a token pair renders with no colour value ever leaving the stylesheet.
WF-017's own module docstring records that its is_valid_colour grammar is wider than intended: a bare 3-20 letter word is accepted, so inherit, initial, unset and javascript all pass.
evidence_for_b: WF-017 already ships per-room colour-valued branding, so the product would then hold two override shapes.
evidence_for_c: A tenant could express anything the CSS parser allows, at the cost of an injection surface and a palette nothing can verify.
state.measurement: backend/tests/test_wf138.py carries eight tests over the token map, including a parametrised refusal of #10506f, #fff, rgb(16,80,111), hsl(200, 40%, 20%) and a named colour, and a refusal of all four product-locked tokens on both sides of a pair. The page offers only selects over the token names, and asserts that no colour input exists.

verdict.instructions: Which model should WF-138 adopt for a tenant brand override?

criteria.adopt_token_to_token: Map token to token. The product keeps the palette and the contrast floor, a tenant can never inject a value, and a later theme change still reaches every tenant.
criteria.prefer_colour_values: Store a validated colour value per token, as WF-017 does per room, and accept that a tenant can opt out of the palette.
criteria.prefer_stylesheet: Let a tenant supply custom properties or a stylesheet.

decision: Implementation of WF-138 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-138 adds a branded room on the customer's own domain as a feature plugin: 20 routes on /api/wf-138, a pure domain module in dsr/competitive_baseline/branded_domain.py, a feature module with the writing service and seed() in dsr/features/wf138_branded_custom_domain.py, two backend test modules, and a frontend page under frontend/src/features/wf-138-branded-domain/. A brand belongs to an account and carries the owner identity, a white-label switch and tenant token overrides; a room joins a brand, inherits its current tokens, and a token change is propagated to every room of the brand in the same request. A tenant override is a token-to-token mapping and never a colour value, so a tenant cannot opt out of a later theme change. No shared file is edited.

declared_unverified: No TLS certificate is issued and no reverse proxy is configured, so a branded https URL was never opened in a browser. The page is exercised by its own frontend tests against stubbed responses, and the API by tools/verify_all_routes.py over http on 127.0.0.1. The product needs infrastructure this repository does not own; /config and /resolve return that list as cannot_verify and the page renders it.
No DNS TXT challenge, so domain verification proves a CNAME exists and not that the account controls the domain. A verified CNAME is necessary and not sufficient, and the code says so.
No per-customer DNS and no CDN edge, so host resolution was never exercised by a real proxy forwarding a Host header; the route takes the resolved host as a parameter and the rule is tested purely.
No DAM or headless CMS for brand assets: a brand asset is a URL string in the brand's own open object, and nothing is uploaded, transcoded or served. The drag-and-drop design tool does not ship.

The whole frontend suite reported one timeout in src/test/wf001-room-templates.test.jsx, a file this change does not touch; it passes when run on its own. It is machine contention on this workstation, and CI 'Frontend build' passed.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
